subjects.displayTitle: Imam Husayn: remembrance, fidelity, and the meaning of victory
subjects.introduction: By what measure can anyone weep for Husayn? The Báb asks it in a visitation prayer and answers that all the seas of creation would not suffice, and that confession is where remembrance begins. Bahá’u’lláh then turns the question back on the mourner: people lament the oppression of the Prince of Martyrs every year and curse his killers, while inflicting a tyranny beside which the old tyranny is nothing. They slay Husayn and then weep for him. Remembrance, in other words, is only true when it changes the one who remembers. Against this stands the paradox at the heart of Karbila: Yazíd had his empire and Husayn his thirst and a body torn to pieces, yet it was the abasement in the desert that became the glory of both worlds, and the shrines the Umayyads and Abbasids ploughed under were found again. Qur’án 2:154 asks that those slain in God’s path not be called dead, for they live in a way observers do not perceive [1]. From here the path leads into the family of Muḥammad and the Imamate, into martyrdom, and into lamentation and grief as schools of fidelity.
subjects.arc: Begin with the limits and responsibilities of remembrance, enter the accounts of suffering, and consider enduring life and the transformation of conduct.

order.why: Read the remembrance as instruction in divine love.
shortened: O thou who art assured of the Divine Manifestation! His Holiness the Prince of Martyrs (may the spirit of all existence be sacrificed for Him) offered up His life in the field of sacrifice on the plain of Karbila, and freely and generously sacrificed His soul and heart and kindred and children and all His possessions in the path of the All-Merciful, that He might teach the friends of God the way of divine love and impart to His spiritual companions the mysteries of the love of God.

order.why: Open with the limits of another person’s understanding of suffering.
shortened: How great is thy station, how sublime thy rank, how momentous thy tragedy, how grievous thy affliction! By what measure shall I weep for thee, and for which of thy calamities shall I lament? Were I to weep with the waters of all the seas of creation and lament with all that is possible in invention, it would not equal an atom of what God decreed for thee of tribulation. Indeed, all others perceive the magnitude of thy tragedy according to the limitations of their own existence, yet they cannot truly know its reality as thou hast experienced it in the path of thy Lord.

order.why: Ask whether mourning changes the mourner’s conduct.
shortened: Observe those who every year lament and wail over the oppression of the Prince of Martyrs - may the spirit of all else but Him be sacrificed for His sake - and His companions, and who curse the oppressors, while they themselves have manifested such tyranny that the oppression of former tyrants is as pure nothingness in comparison.

order.why: Hear the stark warning against harming and then lamenting.
Question what worldly victory and loss finally amount to.
shortened: What advantage did the wicked Yazid derive from his vast empire and limitless pomp and yet what loss and disadvantages befell the Prince of martyrs, Imam Husayn, the Master of the wronged ones of the world, in his homelessness, his suffering, his imprisonment, his captivity and finally with his martyrdom.

order.why: Consider abasement transformed into enduring glory.
shortened: The abasement and lowliness of the Prince of Martyrs (may my spirit be sacrificed for him) in the desert of Karbila was the glory of both worlds and sovereignty of both realms.

order.why: Read eternal life beside outward martyrdom.
shortened: Although that wronged one of the field of calamity, the martyr of Karbila (may the spirit of those nigh unto God be his ransom), in the beginning took the poisoned arrow, in the end, it was his everlasting glory that became well-known and established, and he was destined to attain eternal life in the world that abideth forever.

order.why: Hear the reported meaning of victory despite bodily destruction.
shortened: The Prince of Martyrs in Karbala had his body torn to pieces, yet was still victorious, for "verily it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers."

order.why: Keep the explicit affirmation of physical martyrdom visible.
Distinguish the spiritual station described as beyond injury.
shortened: Know that Hussein has a station where no one can wrong him or usurp his right, as the Imam said in the hadith. How could it not be so when God's side cannot be wronged and God's sovereignty cannot be overcome? He is God's manifestation in creation and the face of the Worshipped One in the beginning and the end.

order.why: Enter the language of devotion and detachment.
shortened: I have turned toward Thee, O Mystery of the Torah and the Gospel, and Dawning-Place of the verses of God, the Mighty, the Beautiful! Through Thee was built the city of detachment and was raised the banner of righteousness upon the highest peaks. Were it not for Thee, the fragrance of divine knowledge would have been cut off from the realm of possibility and the breeze of the All-Merciful from all lands.

order.why: Read Husayn within the prayer’s remembrance of Muhammad’s family.
Hear the testimony of a visitation prayer.
shortened: O my Lord, O Abu 'Abdu'llah! I testify that Thou wert the Illuminator of lights in the worlds of holiness and mysteries, and that when the light of Thy body shone forth upon the land of the Euphrates in this world, the essences in the worlds of realities were kindled, and the verities in the material worlds were established, and all atoms bore witness with the testimony decreed by the Divine Essence that He is exalted above all names and attributes.

order.why: Consider the significance attributed to visiting with recognition.
shortened: And how could it be otherwise, when God's conclusive proof has made the excellence of visiting your praised shrine equal to visiting Husayn, peace be upon him, even though no excellence in the heavens or earth equals his? For he said - may my spirit and all in the kingdom of creation and command be sacrificed for him - "Whoever visits Husayn, peace be upon him, knowing his true station, is like one who has visited God above His throne."

order.why: Keep the Bab’s specific directive in its historical setting.
Clarify whom the visitation prayer names.
Read the affirmation of continuing love and lamentation.
shortened: For the people are ignorant, indolent, unknowing, and heedless, and may imagine, God forbid, that the friends have grown remiss or deficient in their love for the Prince of the Righteous. Whereas we would lay down our lives in their path, would recite at length the visitation of the Prince of Martyrs, and, when hearing it, would become, like the clouds of springtime, the companions of tearful eyes.

order.why: Hear the recollection of commemoration during Muharram.
shortened: This Wronged One, for successive years in Zawra, during Muharram, did Himself make mention of the tribulations of the Prince of Martyrs, may the souls of all else be a sacrifice unto Him, while the Persians were engaged in lamentation.

order.why: Retain the particular counsel concerning commemorative practice.
Enter the account of departure and encirclement.
shortened: Among them is the true account of Husayn, when he departed from his home with his family and companions, as ye hear tell each day and hour. The hosts of unbelief surrounded them from every side and prevented them from returning to God's sacred sanctuary.

order.why: Hear the concise remembrance of the surrounding enemies.
shortened: His Holiness the Prince of Martyrs (may the spirit of all martyrs be sacrificed for him) was surrounded by enemies on the plain of Karbila.

order.why: Attend to the suffering of Ali son of Husayn within the lament.
shortened: Glory be to God, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe! O God! I pour out my sorrow and grief unto Thee! Alas, alas! Were all creation to gather to comprehend the thirst of 'Ali son of Husayn, peace be upon them, on the day of battle, they would fail. His liver - may my spirit be his sacrifice - had become from thirst like a piece of iron in fire. If they deny, then witness with thine own eyes how he bore the holy struggle with such tremendous thirst.

order.why: Read the source’s account of persecution and the persecutors’ boasting.
shortened: The hostile band and foolish company--that is, the tyrannous and rebellious group--were happy and joyful on the plain of Karbila, constantly boasting before friend and stranger, saying "Praise be to God! The Wronged One of the horizons has been surrounded with his family, their hearts are burning with the heat of thirst, all their possessions have been plundered and pillaged, the blessed body has been torn to pieces, the pure blood has stained the black earth, heads have been raised upon spears, and enemies have risen in strife.

order.why: Remember the captivity of the family after the violence.
shortened: O thou who dwellest in Hadba (Mosul)! Hearken unto the call of this Wronged One Who is imprisoned in 'Akka. Then remember those days when the heedless made captives of the family of the Apostle - those by whose faces Yathrib and Batha were illumined - until they entered spacious Damascus.

order.why: Keep the reported feast metaphor in the context of severe affliction.
shortened: Most resplendent of all was the table of the Prince of Martyrs. In truth, it was a feast wherein every bounty was present - exile on one hand, plunder and pillage on another, the captivity of family and kindred on yet another, and after martyrdom the imprisonment of all and the martyrdom of many. It was a feast wherein every kind of food was present. Then the sacred household was taken captive and the holy heads were carried from city to city atop spears.

order.why: Read the account of the bodies left on the battlefield.
shortened: Consider that they did not bury His Holiness the Prince of Martyrs (may my spirit be sacrificed for him) and all his companions in Muslim cemeteries, but left them covered in blood and mixed with dust in the land of Taff.

order.why: Hear the concise identification of martyrdom at Karbala.
shortened: His holiness, the Prince of Martyrs (Imam Husayn)- blessing and peace rest upon him- became a martyr in the desert of Karbala.

order.why: Consider the wider company remembered in the calamity.
shortened: Consider that in former centuries, certain souls in the desert of Karbila experienced injury and trials and pillage and affliction and supreme martyrdom - may my spirit be sacrificed for them.

order.why: Examine the reported role of hostile stories and accusations.
Compare the justifications given for persecution in different settings.
Read the appeal to judge the wronged ones fairly.
shortened: Did my Hasan deal faithlessly amongst you, unlawfully devour your wealth, or shed your blood? Judge ye fairly, O people, and be not of them that speak falsely! Explain ye, O people of the Furqan! For what crime did ye slay my Husayn in the Land of Sad?"

order.why: Keep the later Hasan and Husayn within their own occasion.
shortened: This is the year wherein Hasan sacrificed himself in the path of God, the Lord of the worlds, and after him Husayn, who attained the most great martyrdom.

order.why: Read a renewed tale of sacrifice in the visitation of a later martyr.
shortened: Blessed is he who visits My Name Husayn, concerning whom My Most Exalted Pen has spoken, and who says before his grave:

"By God! Through you the tale of sacrifice was renewed, and the Concourse on High lamented, and the Lote-Tree of the Far Boundary cried out. Blessed is the soul that turned to you and visited your dust and remembered your days and what befell you from the enemies of the Self of God, your Lord.

order.why: Consider the comparison with the suffering of the Apostle’s family.
shortened: O Scions of that House! Verily, there hath come upon you in the path of God that which came upon the descendants of the Apostle and their women and children in the Land of Taff [Karbila] and elsewhere.

order.why: Read the language of return applied to a woman’s afflictions.
shortened: In truth thou art a manifestation of the return of the wife of the Prince of Martyrs Imam Husayn [Shahr-Banu]. Like thee that wronged one of the world was afflicted with mighty calamities; like thee she suffered grievous wrongs.

order.why: Hear the prayer’s symbolic connection with Cain and his victim.
Keep the name Husayn within the speaker’s own prayer of affliction.
shortened: Glorified is He Who hath left Husayn to make His dwelling amidst the hosts of His enemies, and exposed His body with every breath to the spears of hatred and anger; yet do We yield Him thanks for all that He hath destined to befall His Servant Who repaireth unto Him in His affliction and grief.

order.why: Read the Bab’s extended interweaving of Joseph, Husayn, and recognition.
shortened: The All-Merciful intended by the mention of Joseph the very soul of the Prophet and fruit of the Virgin, Husayn son of Ali son of Abu Talib, as witnessed.

What aileth you, O hosts of Satan? Did not the Truth come to you upon his steed on the Day of Ashura, after he had proclaimed unto you, in truth and by the truth, God's most great Cause from his own self, with utmost intensity? Did he not humbly seek water for himself and for his infant child, prostrate upon the earth in sublime truth, weak in that mighty Cause?

order.why: Consider the cited tradition within the argument about recognition.
shortened: For they are ignorant and know not that the Dawning-Place of verses and the Manifestation of clear proofs hath appeared and speaketh. Moreover, they are heedless of the traditions that they themselves consider authentic, such as the saying of the Prince of Martyrs - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for his sake - that after the Qa'im, One bearing the name Qayyum shall appear and all the Prophets and chosen ones shall gather beneath His shadow.

order.why: Hear the proclamation of return in a new appearance.
shortened: Say: By God! This is Husayn Who hath appeared among you in truth with a holy and wondrous beauty, with mighty signs of attraction, with delicate melodies of the spirit, and with sweet strains of love - yet ye recognized not His worth, nor hearkened to His melodies, nor perceived His beauty, nor attained unto the radiant beauty of His light.

order.why: Read the challenge to recognize present sacrifice.
shortened: They counted the martyrdom of Husayn ibn 'Ali as a mighty proof of the manifestation of the Seal of the Prophets, yet they remain heedless and veiled from that which has come to pass in these days. Say: This is Husayn Who hath appeared after the Qa'im.

order.why: Consider the reported comparison between earlier and later martyrs.
Ask what it means for living water to meet no thirst.
Hear the recollected appeal for aid.
shortened: On the day of His martyrdom on the field of Karbala, Husayn ibn `Ali spoke these words: "Is there anyone truly capable of dispensing victory who will come to aid me?"

order.why: Keep the Bab’s vision distinct from a historical description.
shortened: In My vision I saw the head of the Imam Husayn, the Siyyidu'sh-Shuhada', which was hanging upon a tree. Drops of blood dripped profusely from His lacerated throat.

order.why: Attend to the separate figure of Ali ibn Husayn.
shortened: Follow the example of Ali ibn Husayn, peace be upon him. Hassan of Basra relates that one day in the desert of Hijaz, I observed from the direction of the wilderness that a radiant youth of perfect beauty and grace was coming, wandering and searching, but with bare head, bare feet and naked body.

order.why: Read the contrast between enduring glory and temporal power.
shortened: Consider how the abasement of His Holiness the unique martyr, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was what eternal glory, while the glory of the wicked Yazid and the rebellious Walid became what abasement and degradation in the eternal world - even in this mortal world.

order.why: Consider the days of adversity as the center of remembrance.
shortened: Consider how the Prince of Martyrs lived in the world for many tranquil years but it is the significance of his calamities borne from dawn until dusk, which are of such consequence. Hast thou ever heard mention of his other days? Nay, rather all remembrance of that luminous being is restricted to his days of suffering and adversity in the land of Karbila.

order.why: Hear the reported persistence of grief across generations.
shortened: How many kings are killed but there is no mention of them, but when one person is killed in the path of God how much dignity they have, how much radiance they have, how much grandeur they have. For one thousand three hundred years the Prince of Martyrs was killed, and still lamentations and cries are raised for him.

order.why: Compare lasting signs with vanished palaces.
shortened: All their palaces and royal residences are ruined and not one trace is left behind; but the signs of the Master of the Martyrs, Imam Hossein are clear and manifest, even in this mortal world.

order.why: Read the brief contrast between two lives that both ended.
Keep the account of attempts to erase the shrine attributed to its reported source.
Consider the fruits of sacrifice in the language of light and a garden.
Hear the devotional account of sweetness within unbearable trial.
shortened: The trials of the desert of Karbila were unbearable, but in the palate of the Prince of Martyrs (may my spirit and the spirit of all be sacrificed for him) they were most sweet.

order.why: Read the question of accepting no ransom.
Keep the poetic summons to the Karbala of love as an image of fidelity.
Consider consolation that questions the highest value placed on ease.
shortened: Yet be not saddened, neither be thou sick at heart: for if placidity of heart, tranquillity of spirit, and bodily repose were truly beloved, praiseworthy and desirable, His Holiness the Prince of Martyrs would assuredly have sought and yearned after them; while all the Prophets and holy ones would have chosen them for themselves.

order.why: Read the reported yearning to have shared the earlier ordeal.
shortened: One of the ulama of Simnan during his governorship, whenever there was a gathering commemorating the martyrdom and suffering of the Lord of Martyrs, would repeatedly say with great anguish "Would that I had been with thee and attained a mighty triumph!"

order.why: Keep the brief scene of lamentation in its limited supplied context.
shortened: I observed a group of people, grief-stricken and heartbroken, weeping and lamenting, engaged in reciting elegies for the Prince of Martyrs (peace be upon him), crying out: "O Husayn, what did they do when they made thee a sacrifice!" I said, "Glory be to God!

order.why: Reflects on mourning for Imam Husayn and the repetition of persecution.
Hear the warning about joy taken in another’s suffering.
shortened: They rejoice in what they have wrought, even as those who slew Husayn rejoiced. Take ye warning, and be not of them that understand not.

order.why: Read the counsel to answer reproach with reasonableness.
shortened: If someone face to face reproaches or taunts you, say with perfect reasonableness: "The honored martyrs followed the example of the martyrs of the plain of Karbila. Would that I had been with them to achieve a great achievement!" It has always been thus - there is nothing new. "This is not the first flask that has been broken in Islam."

order.why: Consider restraint when faced with vehement speech.
shortened: When they speak with vehemence, maintain a oppressed silence, and if they reproach with moderation or relate tales, say that this is a recognition of the plain of Karbila and commemoration of the Prince of Martyrs, and this is the glory and pride of the people of God.

order.why: End with the Bab’s summons toward the covenant of an Imam described as God’s servant.

questions: What different meanings of victory emerge when worldly power is read beside fidelity and enduring remembrance?
How does the warning about people who mourn oppression while inflicting it change the work of commemoration?
What can lamentation express, and what limits does the visitation passage place on understanding another’s suffering?
How do the references to later martyrs and spiritual return deepen the remembrance while requiring careful attention to distinct persons?
How does Qur’an 2:154 illuminate the relationship between bodily death and the life these passages describe?
What qualities in speech, conduct, and treatment of others might show that remembrance has become a source of moral transformation?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 2:154 · Life beyond what is perceived
references.note: Pickthall’s translation asks readers not to call those slain in God’s way dead, affirming a life that observers do not perceive. Read this beside the compilation’s simultaneous acknowledgment of physical martyrdom and affirmation of enduring spiritual life. How does the distinction reshape the meaning of defeat, grief, and remembrance?

subjects.displayTitle: The importance of prayer: attention, dependence, and action
subjects.introduction: Prayer is like a song, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, made of words and melody together, and sometimes it is the melody that moves us. Words without love mean nothing. Yet the practice He describes is anything but vague. It has a daily rhythm, with obligatory prayer at its heart and remembrance at dawn, midnight and evening; it polishes the dust from the mirror of the heart; and it lifts the spirit on two wings out of the lowest depths. Nor does it replace effort. Prayer is the spirit and means are the hand, and to abandon the means is to seek to quench thirst without water, so work and worship go hand in hand. Jesus’ warning against praying for display and trusting in many words sharpens the point that attention, not volume, is what God receives [1]. The way leads onward into the law of obligatory prayer, the power and the inner state of prayer, and the trust in God that lets a person turn to Him at all times.
subjects.arc: Begin with the quality of prayer, connect devotion with practical means, and follow remembrance into daily rhythms, service, and sustained action.

order.why: Place love and attachment before mechanical speech.
shortened: "Prayer need not be in words, but in thought and attitude. But if this love and this desire are lacking it is useless to try to force them. Words without love mean nothing. If a person talks to you as an unpleasant duty with no love or pleasure in his meeting with you, do you wish to converse with him? Efforts should first be made to make attachment to God."

order.why: Open with prayer as both attitude and word.
Connect prayer with the practical means through which action occurs.
shortened: Concerning means and prayer about which thou didst inquire: Prayer is like unto the spirit, and means are like unto the hand. The spirit's control is exercised through the hand.

But to abandon means is like unto one who is thirsty seeking to quench his thirst without water or other liquids. The Bestower and Creator of water is the Almighty Lord, and He hath made it the means of quenching thirst.

order.why: Hold work and prescribed worship together.
Hear the purpose expressed in the short obligatory prayer.
shortened: I bear witness, O my God, that Thou hast created me to know Thee and to worship Thee. I testify, at this moment, to my powerlessness and to Thy might, to my poverty and to Thy wealth. There is none other God but Thee, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Consider prayer as water that gives life and joy.
shortened: O thou daughter of the Kingdom!  Know thou that supplication and prayer is the Water of Life.  It is the cause of the vivification of existence, and endows glad-tidings and joy to the souls.  Show thou attention to this matter as far as thou canst, and summon others to prayer and supplication.

order.why: Read the heart’s polishing and growing taste for devotion.
shortened: Man becomes like a stone unless he continually supplicates to GOD. The heart of man is like a mirror that is covered with dust, and to cleanse it one must continually pray to GOD that it may become clean, and the act of supplication is the polish which erases all worldly desires. The delight of supplicating and entreating before GOD cuts one's heart from the world. When the taste of man is nourished by honey, he never likes to taste any other sweetmeat. Therefore, prayer is a key by which the doors of the kingdom are opened.

order.why: Explore the image of wings and inward tranquility.
shortened: The human heart finds no tranquility except through worship of the All-Merciful, and the human spirit finds no joy except through remembrance of God. The power of worship is like wings that cause the human spirit to ascend from the lowest depths to the Abha Kingdom and bestow true purity and refinement upon human beings. The goal cannot be attained except through this means.

order.why: Hear the related image of prayer and supplication as two wings.
Consider the continuing prayerful attitude.
Read the attraction and awakening of the state of prayer.
Join spiritual thirst with study, prayer, meditation, and living.
Turn supplication toward justice and rebuilding the world.
Join humility with becoming a servant of reconciliation.
Read invocation together with loving service.
shortened: Know that nothing will benefit thee in this life save supplication and invocation unto God, service in His vineyard, and, with a heart full of love, be in constant servitude unto Him.

order.why: Hold hope for the eternal world beside adorning this one.
Move from recitation to helping others find direction.
shortened: Recite thou the verses of guidance. Be engaged in the worship of thy Lord, and rise up to lead the people aright.

order.why: Place devotions alongside teaching and the education of children.
shortened: Let them strive with wisdom to guide receptive souls, endeavor to educate children according to divine commandments, and arise to perform prayer, supplication, fasting and devotions as required by God's decisive command.

order.why: Hear a prayer for remembrance and service together.
shortened: Hold fast to the cord of thy Lord's loving-kindness and say: O Thou through Whom the horizon of the world was illumined and the hearts of the nations were shaken! I beseech Thee by Thy Most Exalted Word and by Thy Most Luminous and Most Glorious Countenance to aid me in Thy remembrance and praise and in serving Thy Cause, and to ordain for me what Thou hast ordained for the best among Thy creatures.

order.why: Read the personal account of consolation through repeated prayer.
Keep the reported counsel in its devotional and personal setting.
shortened: The Master - Whenever you feel depressed, go alone into the secret chamber, read one of the Hidden Words and with the utmost supplication beg of Baha'u'llah to impart to you that happiness which is essential for the future. Pray with great humbleness:
O God, free me from these fetters.

order.why: Read the encouragement concerning the effect of prayers.
shortened: Read my prayers always and thus see a wonderful effect, causing all superstitious powers and influences to vanish away.

order.why: Keep the language of healing within its devotional context.
shortened: Say: Through His remembrance is every sick one healed of his illness and the hearts of those who have turned to Him are purified.

order.why: Consider remembrance as the removal of inward darkness.
shortened: For the remembrance of God removeth all darkness from the hearts of His servants and rendereth them sanctified from all else besides Him.

order.why: Read the relation between nearness and illumination.
shortened: Supplication causes one to draw nigh unto the precincts of His divinity and to beseech the help of God illumines one's spirit.

order.why: Consider turning toward the shrine beyond physical distance.
shortened: Turn to the Holy Shrine and whatever you seek will be answered. This turning has no nearness or remoteness - one can turn from any spot or any clime, for the Sanctuary of the Supreme Concourse encompasses all created things and is raised up in the Most Exalted Station.

order.why: Attend to the stated center of orientation in prayer.
shortened: In prayer one must turn his face towards the Sanctified Reality of His holiness Baha’u’llah—that Reality which surrounds all the phenomena. During the time of prayer His Holiness Baha’u’llah must be singly and alone the center towards whom all the faces are turned.

order.why: Join remembrance with steadfast devotion and worship.
shortened: Make mention of thy Lord, then be thou steadfast in devotion, and bow down in worship.

order.why: Read the obligation beginning at maturity.
Connect prescribed prayer and fasting with remembrance and awareness of need.
Hear the invitation to share the spiritual outpouring at dawn.
Consider waking early from longing rather than display.
Read midnight and dawn as times of invocation.
shortened: Supplicate to God, pray to Him and invoke Him at midnight and at dawn.

order.why: Keep the recurring rhythm through darkness, morning, and evening.
Consider purification of attention at different times of day.
shortened: Purify thyself from all remembrance, then remember thy Lord at eventide and at dawn, and in the morning and in the evening.

order.why: Hear the promise accompanying remembrance at evening and dawn.
Read recurring remembrance as a continuing orientation.
Attend to the specific invocation at dawn.
shortened: Turn to the Lord of the Kingdom and in the early hours of dawn engage in the mention of Ya Baha'u'l-Abha.

order.why: Consider the invitation to pray at all times.
shortened: It is incumbent upon thee to turn unto the Kingdom of God and to pray, supplicate and invoke during all times.

order.why: Join recognition with the value of remembrance.
shortened: O handmaid of God! Praise the Beloved of the world that you have attained to His recognition and are gazing at His horizon. Know the value of this station and be occupied with His remembrance at all times, detached from all else.

order.why: Read gratitude expressed through love and faithfulness.
shortened: Now, in gratitude for this bounty and favor, thou must occupy thyself with love and faithfulness, be engaged day and night in the remembrance of God, and be occupied in humble entreaty and supplication. Thou must recite the verses of divine unity and be raised up with the essence of sanctification.

order.why: Hear praise in response to being remembered.
shortened: Rejoice in that thy name hath flowed from the Most Exalted Pen. This is indeed a great bounty. Glorify thy Lord with praise at all times and say: Praise be unto Thee, O Beloved of the worlds and Goal of all who are in the heavens and on earth.

order.why: Consider the value attributed to divine remembrance of a person.
shortened: Rejoice thou in My remembrance of thee. Nothing in the kingdom can equal it, as doth testify He with Whom is the knowledge of all things in a clear Book.

order.why: Retain the particular affirmation addressed to a woman.
shortened: Verily she who has believed in her Lord is better than men in the Tablet of God, the Lord of the worlds. Give thanks to your Lord, then remember Him at all times.

order.why: Read gratitude within the addressee’s distinct circumstances.
Make room for heartfelt and tearful praise.
Hear the invitation to melody and thanksgiving.
shortened: Take a firm step and chant prayers with the melody of the Abha Kingdom. Open your tongues in thanksgiving.

order.why: Consider recitation as a song and fragrance.
Read devotion that draws other hearts.
Hear the language of finding solace and hearing the call.
Consider diligence in the prayers already at hand.
Read humility and intimacy with remembrance together.
shortened: As much as you can, show humility and supplication at the threshold of the Most Glorious Beauty, and be intimate with the mention of the Most Great Name (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him).

order.why: Hear the repeated seeking of assistance.
Let the prayer ask to become familiar with humility and need.
shortened: O servant of Truth, open thy tongue in prayer and with the utmost supplication and entreaty, show forth humility and need at the threshold of the All-Glorious Lord, saying: "O peerless God! Make Thou a way that I may become intimate and familiar with humility and need, and with a plaintive voice raise my supplications to the highest heaven.

order.why: Read shared supplication for servitude and steadfastness.
shortened: Day and night I will stretch forth the hand of supplication and pray - you too supplicate and implore, so that through the power of utter helplessness and lamentation we may take our place in servitude and remain firm and steadfast in the Covenant.

order.why: Consider the counsel to pray with humility day and night.
Consider invocation and communion as a continuing pathway.
Hear the prayer for another’s continuing remembrance.
Read communion as something shared across separation.
Consider prayer on another’s behalf for forgiveness and favor.
shortened: I read your letter and I will beseech and implore at the threshold of the One, that the forgiveness of the Forgiving Lord may encompass you and the favors of the Desired One may surround you.

order.why: Hear the remembrance of another person’s devotion.
Read prayer within a particular period of waiting for deliverance.
shortened: Spend thy time in humble supplication, intimate prayer and devotion to the Fulfiller of needs until God brings deliverance from those quarters.

Join prayer, service, and spiritual joy.
shortened: Night and day we were engaged in prayer and supplication and service at the Threshold of the Lord of Verses. We were serving with some measure of freedom and praying for all, detached from any mention save the mention of God, and had attained some spiritual joy.

order.why: Keep the specific counsel about company, business, and supplication in context.
shortened: Certainly, absolutely be free from such a detestable group and occupy yourself with trade and business, and continually supplicate and implore at the divine threshold, and pray for our good.

order.why: Read spiritual melody through the letter received.
Consider a burning heart that awakens other hearts.
shortened: O thou enkindled leaf!

With a burning heart pray to the Kingdom of Glory by day and by night, commune with Him, and beseech that He may so enkindle thee from His lighted fire that thou mayest become like unto a raging flame and bestir the hearts of the handmaidens of God and enable them to gain detachment.

shortened: They raised the hands of supplication toward the heaven of Mercy, communed with their Maker and longed for the appearance of these Days.

Begin supplied readings with the seed nourished through a whole spiritual life.
Consider purity of heart within the account of guidance.

Place the six stated practices in their integrated relationship.
Keep the reported distinction among prayer, meditation, study, and action.
Read action and example as tangible fruits.
Consider the sequence of prayer, reflection, study, and perseverance.
End with sustained action as part of the practice.

How can regular or obligatory prayer remain an expression of love and attention?
What does the relationship between prayer and practical means suggest about dependence and responsibility?
How does Matthew 6:5–8 challenge performance or reliance on many words, and how might that deepen a repeated practice?
How do personal consolation and the desire for justice and peace meet in these readings?

subjects.displayTitle: Interpreting dreams: symbols, context, and patient understanding
subjects.introduction: A fish in one dream is the attainment of a desire; in another the fish are souls swimming in the sea of this lower world, waiting to be drawn up in the net of love; in a third they are old superstitions transformed into true beliefs. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá interpreted dreams with great tenderness and no fixed code, reading each image for the person who dreamed it. Sometimes He deferred altogether, saying the time to understand had not come; Bahá’u’lláh warned that no one may test God with a dream and allowed that a vision might be mixed with fancy. Often the meaning given is simply growth: ascent is deepening love and knowledge, milk is wisdom, a spacious house is the inward freedom of those who outwardly sit in prison. Joseph read Pharaoh’s dreams and then organised the granaries, and that turn from symbol to responsibility is worth keeping in view [1]. From here the path leads into the dream accounts themselves, into why such visions matter, and into who may interpret with authority and how prophecy differs from private reassurance.
subjects.arc: Begin with symbols whose meanings depend on context, examine patience and discernment, and follow interpretation toward growth, service, and response.

order.why: Consider a third use of fish within transformed clouds.
shortened: The dream thou hadst seen hath this interpretation: The rising of the brilliant star is the appearance of the Blessed Beauty, and the dispersal of the clouds into variegated fish means that clouds which prevent the sun from appearing are the ancient superstitions and beliefs which have been transformed into correct truths, and these correct beliefs are the fish of the sea of truth.

order.why: Open with a particular interpretation of water and fish.
Read a different meaning given to fish in another vision.
Allow the time for understanding to remain open.
shortened: The time for the interpretation of the dream has not yet come. Reflect and it will become clear and evident.

order.why: Read ascent as growth in love and knowledge.
Explore sun, water, and waves through the addressee’s dream.
shortened: As for that mighty solar orb which thou didst behold in thy dream, that was the Promised One, and its spreading rays were His bounties, and the translucent surface of the mass of water signifieth hearts that are undefiled and pure, while the surging waves denote the great excitement of those hearts and the fact that they were shaken and deeply moved, that is, the waves are the stirrings of the spirit and holy intimations of the soul.

order.why: Hear the particular meanings of a sequence of images.
shortened: As for the dreams you saw: Being present in the prayer place indicates entry into the Kingdom of God; sitting indicates steadfastness; drinking milk symbolizes knowledge and wisdom; eating fruits represents discovering questions of truth; and the spring of Tasnim is eternal life.

order.why: Consider the stated interpretation through opposites in its own context.
Acknowledge anxiety that required reassuring news.
Read the warning against making a dream a test of God.
shortened: And concerning thy question about the dream - none hath the right to test God. We shall interpret it for thee as a bounty from Us, and shall reveal unto thee what We showed thee. Be thou assured and be of those who render thanks.

order.why: Keep the possibility of fancy and the attention to outward evidence visible.
Distinguish spiritual discoveries from physical events.
shortened: All that the disciples observed of the appearance of Moses and Elias with Christ on the mountaintop, and the servant's vision of the fiery horses, as well as Peter's vision of the angels of heaven - all these were spiritual discoveries and luminous realities, not physical realities, even in their most subtle form....

order.why: Hear the distinction between a dream and spiritual unveiling.
shortened: O you who are firm in the Covenant! You had asked for the interpretation of your dream. This was not a dream, but rather a spiritual unveiling and divine vision.

order.why: Distinguishes true dreams, dreams requiring interpretation and confused imaginings.
Read the reported vision in prayer through nearness and the heart as mirror.
shortened: As for your vision of this servant in your prayer, this is evidence of spiritual nearness, spiritual unity, and mystical impression. At all times I implore the divine Kingdom to make your heart a pure, delicate, polished mirror facing the Abha Kingdom so that the images of the Supreme Concourse may be reflected in it.
The repetition of the vision indicates that the seeing will be both spiritual and physical.

order.why: Consider consolation in the interpretation of a daughter’s appearance.
shortened: Abdul-Baha said: "The cause of her surprise is this-that you are crying; your daughter would say: 'I have a good mother. She must be happy. Why does she cry? I am surprised.' The cause of her surprise is the thought that you do not recognize her. She belongs to a realm in which everything becomes mature, and she expected you to see her in the state of perfection in which she manifested herself to you; but the fact that you looked at her in this way, and that now you are crying-is a proof of your not having recognized her. For had you recognized her in the dream, you would not be crying now."

order.why: Let humor and hospitality give the vision a human setting.
Retain the childhood dream and its interpreter as a reported account.
Read the dream of birds and a ship without supplying an absent explanation.
Keep the brief statement of clarity within its limited context.
Consider the interval between a dream and a reported fulfillment.
shortened: Although this victory was given as glad tidings in the world of dreams, yet when it was delayed, some were overcome with doubt, but when Mecca was conquered the friends became joyous.

order.why: Read the stated limits of a brief interpretation.
Hear another explicit limit on the detail offered.
shortened: You had related three dreams, for which I will write a brief interpretation as there is no time for detail.

order.why: Consider a paper whose meaning is not yet understood.
Read becoming Adam as a particular account of human perfection.
Hear the spring of Job and alchemy in their symbolic setting.
Consider the transformation of troubled hands through the scriptural image.
Read water falling from Tablets as life in the teachings.
Explore clothing, gems, and lamps through the supplied interpretation.
shortened: His white vestment is the garment of the Manifestation and [His] brilliant color. Regarding the gems which appeared on His breast, they are peerless pearls of wisdom which shine unto the horizons with a godlike fame. As to His shining face, verily it hath illumined the earth and dispersed the darkness from the contingent world. Regarding thine entrance with thy friend into the gallery lighted with lamps, know thou that gallery is the world of humanity and the lamps His wonderful teaching, His all-wisdom, His perfect bounty and His clear manifestation.

order.why: Consider the removal of coverings in relation to rumors.
shortened: Regarding the dream whose interpretation you requested - its interpretation is this: entering the sea naked and bare indicates that, God willing, the reality of God's Cause will become manifest and evident without any veil or covering, and be purified and sanctified from the contamination of the calumnies of the calumniators and the spreaders of false rumors.

order.why: Retain the related interpretation with its visible intervening gap.
Keep the interpretation of names and numbers in its particular address.
Read the tree, lion, woman, and rooster within the Covenant setting.
shortened: The interpretation of the dream which thou didst have is this: That mighty tree is the Blessed Tree and the goodly Tree which has its roots in the earth and its branches in heaven. That frightful creature is one who raised a loud cry and clamor and outwardly clung to the Blessed Tree. That brave lion is the Lion of the Covenant who with one movement caused that creature filled with hatred to fall to the ground, and the Blessed Tree remained established in its place. That woman who was above the tree is the Law of God, and the rooster is the Divine Herald, indicating that the Cause of God will reach the utmost degree of aspiration.

order.why: Connect lofty steps with spiritual growth and unity.
Read new life and the figure of a country in two different dreams.
shortened: That water which came to the house in the world of dreams is that new life, and "from water We made all things living." And that agitation is joy and tranquility and repose.

And as for your second dream, it indicates that the penetration of the Word of God will become intense in Iran, nay rather in all the horizons. And that elderly person is the country of Iran, and the answer to his petition is divine confirmations and assistance.

order.why: Keep the scriptural reference within this interpretation of opposition.
shortened: O thou whose breath is fragrant with musk! The interpretation of the dream is this: that certain souls will strive to extinguish the Fire of God that has been kindled, but through their efforts the flame will grow mightier and the penetrating power of the Word of God will increase. It will become clear and evident that Christ remained unharmed, and "they slew him not, neither crucified him, but it appeared so unto them."

order.why: Retain the specific interpretation given to red cotton.
shortened: And convey my longing greetings to Jinab-i-Aqa Haydar-'Ali and tell him that this dream which you saw is evidence that the red cotton is, God willing, martyrdom in the most glorious path.

order.why: Read the verses and polemical setting without generalizing to other dreams.
shortened: The dream you saw is a remedy for every ailing sufferer, but a thousand proofs cannot overcome the vain imaginings of any Covenant-breaker, for to those of bat-like nature, the brilliant rays of the Sun of Truth cause blindness of sight and provoke anger.

As for the verses revealed in the dream world, the first line is "Open your eyes, raise up the banner" and in the third verse the second line is "The condition of faith is 'God doeth whatsoever He willeth.'"

order.why: Consider the particular interpretation of changing royal attire.
shortened: That the person mentioned was in a carriage with royal majesty and passed before thee, and afterward thou didst meet him with different attire, namely with a turban - there is no doubt that while majesty and royal grandeur are now present and manifest, this change portendeth a transformation of circumstances and an alteration of glory and might. We decree at this time his descent from the first station, that thereby God's servants and creatures might find rest. This is what can be understood from the dream, and hidden knowledge hath thus decreed.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s discussion of Abraham’s vision distinct.
Read the vision of Christ pointing toward light.
shortened: Praise be to God, in the world of dreams you saw rays of light dawning from heaven and Christ pointing with His finger. Know that that light is the dawning of the Sun of Truth and the rays shining from the Abha Beauty.

order.why: Consider the interpretation concerning a house of worship in America.
shortened: This vision showeth that thou, O confirmed and attracted one, by the breezes of God will soon be acquainted with the ancient mysteries, for the Manifest Light will appear to thee. The vision also signifieth that a Mashrak-el-Azcar will soon be established in America.

order.why: Hear the promise of light over a particular region.
Read exaltation of the Cause and the prayer beads in their own setting.
shortened: The interpretation of the dream is that the Cause of God will achieve the utmost exaltation in Iran, especially in Iraq in places connected to them. And seeing the prayer beads indicates that truly these prayer beads were from me.

order.why: Keep the specific prediction concerning Ibn-i-Abhar attributed to its source.
Join confirmation in service with the anticipated spread of the Cause.
shortened: The dream which thou didst see is evidence that through the assistance and favor of the Abha Beauty thou wilt be confirmed in servitude at the Divine Threshold, and the Cause of God will soon achieve a wondrous spread.

order.why: Allow the promised manifestation of meaning to remain in its future tense.
Read weeping interpreted as joy and elevation.
Distinguish outward imprisonment from inward spaciousness.
shortened: This is evidence of God's gifts and bounties bestowed upon you, that you beheld yourself attaining His presence in a spacious place containing many chambers. From time immemorial and unto eternity, the Truth has been and ever shall be in the most exalted and expansive station, and likewise His loved ones--those souls who are sanctified from the doubts and allusions of the veiled ones. Though outwardly they may be seen in prison, in reality they dwell in the highest chambers of paradise, as hath been revealed in the Tablets.

order.why: Connect the dream’s blessing with fulfilling obligations concerning property.
shortened: Regarding the dream you wrote about, it was truly among truthful visions, as the fragrances of love were wafted from it. This indicates that through divine grace and infinite mercy, bounty and blessing shall be bestowed, and you shall fulfill the rights that were due upon your father's property - may the glory and mercy of God rest upon him.

order.why: Turn interpretation toward fresh teaching work.
Read the vision alongside arising to serve.
shortened: Thou hadst a true dream wherein thou didst behold 'Abdu'l-Baha and didst arise to serve the Cause of God. Know thou the value of this bounty and, so long as life remaineth in thy body, render thanks.

order.why: Consider the relation between vision and conduct.
shortened: When thou hast attained to this vision, thou wilt conform all thy movements and rest to the Supreme Concourse, and wilt cry out "Cause me to enter with truth and to depart with truth."

order.why: Hear the instruction to search for truth.
Read humility and love within the vision of Abdu’l-Baha.
shortened: O thou maid-servant of God! Blessed art thou, for the Temple of the Covenant (Abdul-Baha) hath become manifest to thee in a dream with incomparable humility and submission toward God, and that thou hast beheld that countenance overflowing with yearning, attraction and love toward the Beauty of the Almighty. Ere long thou shalt witness a great effect through this observation, whereby the spirit of life will become manifest in thee, which is now flowing in the veins of the contingent beings.

order.why: Consider the qualities named in the interpretation of meeting.
Keep the particular instructions concerning Mrs. Parsons and publication.
shortened: I read the dream - it is well translated. Publish it. This dream indicates that Mrs. Parsons, through divine aid and grace, will attain a state that reveals the divine world, and with the eye of insight will observe those souls who have passed from this world to the next, and spiritual sensations will be produced for her with utmost power.

order.why: Read the affirmation addressed to Mrs. Lina Pontner.
Hear the encouragement addressed to Shoghi.
shortened: O Shoghi, this dream of yours is very good. Rest assured that attaining the presence of His Holiness the Exalted One (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him) is evidence of receiving bounties from the Supreme Lord and attaining the greatest gift and most mighty favor. Likewise for the rest of the dream.

order.why: Consider the blessing attributed to an embrace.
Read the affirmation of a particular vision’s truth.
shortened: As for what thou didst behold in thy dream, give thanks unto God for having revealed Himself unto thee, unveiled to thee His beauty and admitted thee into the pavilion of His glory. Then know thou that what thou didst see is truth, there is no doubt therein, and the matter is as thou didst see.

order.why: Hear the assurance within a period of grief over calumnies.
shortened: O thou whom God hath shown in true visions that which will make his feet firm upon the Straight Path!

By God the True One, verily the heart is in sorrow, and the spirit is in distress, and the inmost heart is in severe pain from what hath befallen the Cause of God through calamities and the spread of calumnies from souls who are turned upside down. Therefore thank God for showing thee the vision, wherein is the greatest wealth [abundance] for a man. By thy life! Verily he is in what God hath shown thee.
That vision was a true vision.

order.why: Keep the brief affirmation in its limited setting.
shortened: O leaf of the Blessed Tree! This dream is true. The chain of servitude to the Blessed Beauty is connected to and associated with the Greatest Name, and the keys are an indication that this chain of servitude is the means of opening doors and is in every way a protection for the heart and soul and a safeguard for the spirit and mind.

order.why: Consider the agreement with the addressee’s interpretation.
Read the concise acknowledgment of a good dream.
shortened: The dream you had was surely a good one.

order.why: Hear gratitude for witnessing signs.
shortened: Thank God that in the world of vision thou art witnessing great signs.

order.why: Retain the clarification concerning the people addressed in a dream.
Read the two dreams through favor and protection.
shortened: Both dreams are evidence that thou art regarded with the glance of favor and art near to the Divine Threshold, and through abundant grace art protected and joyous in the shelter of the All-Forgiving Lord.

order.why: Consider flowers, blossoms, and stars as expressions of bounty.
shortened: Your letter reached this servant and after being presented, the Most Exalted Tongue spoke these lustrous words: That which you saw in your dream was mentioned in the presence. As for what you mentioned about seeing in heaven flowers, blossoms and stars - these indicate the manifestations of your Lord's favors and the expressions of His power.

order.why: Let the prayer ask for the dream’s blessing to be realized.
Read the account of detachment and a journey through spiritual realms.
Hear the invitation to attention, intention, and joy.
End with recognition joined to steadfastness and love.
shortened: Rejoice within thyself for having shown thee in thy dream My hallowed, mighty and resplendent Beauty, even as We showed thee when We were in Iraq, and from My mouth there flowed the Salsabil of thy Lord's wisdom, the Mighty, the Powerful.
Be thou steadfast in the Cause, then stand firm in His love, and He shall suffice thee against all the worlds.

questions: What changes when similar dream images receive different meanings in different contexts?
How do deferred explanations and acknowledged uncertainty affect the responsibilities of an interpreter?
What distinctions do these readings make among spiritual discovery, physical events, personal reassurance, and fancy?
How does Joseph’s interpretation in Genesis 41:25–36 lead toward responsibility and action?
What kinds of growth or service are encouraged by the interpretations in this compilation?
How might a person receive meaning from an experience while remaining patient and careful about claims made for others?

references.label: 1 · Genesis 41:25–36 · Interpretation and preparation
references.note: In the King James Version, Joseph interprets Pharaoh’s paired dreams as years of plenty followed by famine, then proposes storing food under responsible oversight. Read the movement from symbolic interpretation to practical preparation beside the compilation’s invitations to growth and service. Attend also to the distinctive authority and setting of Joseph’s interpretation, rather than taking it as a general method for decoding dreams.

subjects.displayTitle: The divine Educator: bringing hidden capacities into life
subjects.introduction: A lump of coal and a diamond are made of the same thing; what differs is what has been done to it. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá uses that contrast for the work of the Prophets, Who come not to add information to a human being but to bring out what God has already placed there, so that a drop becomes a sea and a wild tree bears fruit. Bahá’u’lláh says that every soul carries a trust it may never discover without a teacher, and that all humankind are children in one school. Their education is of three kinds at once: ordering material life so that people can earn a livelihood, opening the mind to discovery, and lifting the spirit into the moral world. Its proof is conduct, the bloodthirsty turning gentle and the lovers of war seeking peace. Jesus’ invitation to the burdened to learn from One who is meek and lowly of heart puts the teacher’s character at the centre of the same picture [1]. From here the path leads to the Manifestation as gardener and physician, to why humanity needs an educator at all, and to the purpose religion serves in a person and a society.
subjects.arc: Begin with latent capacities, explore the dimensions of divine education, and ask how learning becomes visible in character, service, and civilization.

order.why: Read guidance as awakening awareness of an entrusted inner reality.
shortened: Men at all times and under all conditions stand in need of one to exhort them, guide them and to instruct and teach them.  Therefore He hath sent forth His Messengers, His Prophets and chosen ones that they might acquaint the people with the divine purpose underlying the revelation of Books and the raising up of Messengers, and that every- one may become aware of the trust of God which is latent in the reality of every soul.

order.why: Open with the unfolding of capacities already present in the human reality.
shortened: Through the Teachings of this Daystar of Truth every man will advance and develop until he attaineth the station at which he can manifest all the potential forces with which his inmost true self hath been endowed. It is for this very purpose that in every age and dispensation the Prophets of God and His chosen Ones have appeared amongst men, and have evinced such power as is born of God and such might as only the Eternal can reveal.

order.why: Introduce the school whose education embraces outward and inward life.
Distinguish material, human, and spiritual education.
shortened: Our meaning is that the universal Educator must be at once a material, a human and a spiritual educator, and, soaring above the world of nature, must be possessed of another power, so that He may assume the station of a divine teacher. Were He not to wield such a celestial power, He would not be able to educate, for He would be imperfect Himself. How then could He foster perfection? If He were ignorant, how could He make others wise? If He were unjust, how could He make others just? If He were earthly, how could He make others heavenly?

order.why: Make transformed conduct the practical test of education.
shortened: It is that the portionless should gain their share of the boundless sea, and the ignorant drink their fill from the living fount of knowledge; that those who thirst for blood should forsake their savagery, and those who are barbed of claw should turn gentle and forbearing, and those who love war should seek instead for true conciliation; it is that the brutal, their talons razor-sharp, should enjoy the benefits of lasting peace; that the foul should learn that there is a realm of purity, and the tainted find their way to the rivers of holiness.
Unless these divine bestowals be revealed from the inner self of humankind, the bounty of the Manifestation will prove barren, and the dazzling rays of the Sun of Truth will have no effect whatever.

order.why: Acknowledge lives whose capacities have not found full outward opportunity.
shortened: As to those souls who are born into this life as ethereal and radiant entities and yet, on account of their handicaps and trials, are deprived of great and real advantages, and leave the world without having lived to the full -- certainly this is a cause for grieving. This is the reason why the universal Manifestations of God unveil Their countenances to man, and endure every calamity and sore affliction, and lay down Their lives as a ransom; it is to make these very people, the ready ones, the ones who have capacity, to become dawning points of light, and to bestow upon them the life that fadeth never.

order.why: Read the lighting of a lamp as the release of latent perfections.
Consider wisdom watering what has been deposited within each person.
Read the images of diamond and fruit through human development.
shortened: Should he come under the shadow of the true Educator and be rightly trained, he becomes the gem of gems, the light of lights, and the spirit of spirits; he becomes the focal centre of divine blessings, the wellspring of spiritual attributes, the dawning-place of heavenly lights, and the recipient of divine inspirations. Should he, however, be deprived of this education, he becomes the embodiment of satanic attributes, the epitome of animal vices, and the source of all that is oppressive and dark.

This is the wisdom of the appearance of the Prophets: to educate humanity, that this lump of coal may become a diamond and this barren tree may be grafted and yield fruit of the utmost sweetness and delicacy.

order.why: Consider education’s concern with hidden jewels becoming manifest.
Read the gardener analogy in its historical rhetorical setting.
shortened: A true cultivator changes this forest and jungle into a garden, training its trees to bring forth fruit and causing flowers to grow in place of thorns and thistles. The holy Manifestations are the ideal Gardeners of human souls, the divine Cultivators of human hearts. The world of existence is but a jungle of disorder and confusion, a state of nature producing nothing but fruitless, useless trees. The ideal Gardeners train these wild, uncultivated human trees, cause them to become fruitful, water and cultivate them day by day so that they adorn the world of existence and continue to flourish in the utmost beauty.

order.why: Hear the continuing care given to growing saplings.
Consider nurture through knowledge and understanding.
Explore the need for care and guidance through the child analogy.
Read maturation alongside the image of light.
shortened: The inhabitants of the world are like unto the children. The suckling babes must be nurtured properly so that they may attain to the age of adolescence.
Darkness has surrounded the regions of the world. They must become illumined with this Light of the Kingdom.

order.why: Hear the brief statement of the need for education.
Consider the related image of the world’s Educator.
shortened: They are like unto mere children, and our Lord is the Educator of the world.

order.why: Read the need arising from human imperfection.
Connect the qualification of prophethood with training and guidance.
Hear the concise statement of the prophetic purpose.
shortened: The purpose of the prophetic mission is none other than the education and guidance of the people.

order.why: Ask what actual training results from the mission.
Read the power attributed to the Luminaries in their educational mission.
Distinguish the stations of the Manifestation within this account.
shortened: We stated before that the Manifestations of God have three stations: first, the material reality, which pertains to the human body; second, the individual reality, that is, the rational soul; and third, the heavenly manifestation, which consists in the divine perfections and is the source of the life of the world, the education of the souls, the guidance of the people, and the enlightenment of all creation.

order.why: Consider education of the seen and unseen.
shortened: He is the Quickener of existence and the Educator of the seen and the unseen.

order.why: Hear the devotional naming of the Educator of nations.
Read the mirror as a means of reflecting light and love.
shortened: The mission of the Prophets, the revelation of the Holy Books, the manifestation of the heavenly Teachers and the purpose of divine philosophy all center in the training of the human realities so that they may become clear and pure as mirrors and reflect the light and love of the Sun of Reality.

order.why: Explore the sun analogy for the principles of life.
Consider teachings as rays from the Educator.
Read the claim concerning the advancement of nations.
Ask what the education and progress of people show.
Distinguishes the spiritual education of the Manifestations from material education.
Connect maturity, knowledge, love, and unity.
shortened: All the Prophets of God, including Jesus Christ, appeared in the world for the education of humanity, to develop immature souls into maturity, to transform the ignorant of mankind into the knowing, thereby establishing love and unity through divine education and training.
The Prophets come into the world to guide and educate humanity so that the animal nature of man may disappear and the divinity of his powers become awakened.

order.why: Read spiritual education through the moral world.
shortened: The third kind of education is that of the spirit. Through the breaths of the Holy Spirit man is uplifted into the world of moralities and illumined by the lights of divine bestowals. The moral world is only attained through the effulgence of the Sun of Reality and the quickening life of the divine spirit.

For this reason the holy, divine Manifestations are the first Teachers and Educators of humanity; Their traces are the highest evidences, and Their spiritual tuition is universal in its application to the world of mankind.

order.why: Keep the broad historical and racial judgments attributed to their source.
shortened: It is therefore evident that mankind requires a universal divine educator who can gather the diverse peoples under the shadow of one Word, cause contending nations to drink from a single fountain, transform enmity and hatred into love and fellowship, and convert strife and conflict into peace and tranquility. Thus did the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon Him) unite the warring, hostile, and savage tribes of the Arabian desert and bring them together under the pavilion of unity. As a result, those desert Arabs achieved tremendous progress, raised the banner of perfection in both spiritual and material realms, and attained everlasting glory. Likewise, Christ (peace be upon Him) gathered together the antagonistic, hostile, and warring peoples of Greece, Rome, Syria, Chaldea, and Assyria who were filled with the utmost hatred and enmity, uniting them at one fountain and establishing complete harmony among them.
Thus it is clear and evident that mankind needs a universal educator and teacher, and these are the holy Manifestations of God.

order.why: Read the account of Moses within its theological presentation of history.
shortened: They were the most ignorant of peoples and became the most learned. By virtue of that which He established, they so progressed as to be singled out among all nations, and their fame spread to every land, to such a degree that when the inhabitants of neighbouring lands wanted to praise someone they would say, "Surely he must be an Israelite!" Moses established laws and ordinances that conferred new life upon the people of Israel and led them to attain the highest degree of civilization at that time.

order.why: Consider the reported account of Moses as a teacher of civilization.
Read renewal when the world is described as divided and dark.
Keep Christ’s teaching within the account of His generation.
Explore fatherhood as an image of spiritual education.
shortened: "By the Father we mean the Educator. Just as the Father is tender to his children, likewise, the instructor teaches them. The function of the Father and the Educator is the same. The father gives the material life, the Educator gives the mental and the spiritual life. Therefore when we say Baha'u'llah is the Father, we mean he is an Educator - an spiritual Educator - or in other words, he is the Manifestation of divine attributes.

order.why: Read the account of Baha’u’llah’s work amid conflict.
Consider teaching through speech, writing, and gesture.
shortened: After this Wronged One repaired to Iraq, at all times was He engaged in the education of souls. The tongue spoke, the pen flowed, and gesture and sign were employed. In some instances, We illumined and moved creation through speech. At other times We were occupied in assisting the Cause of God through the pen. And occasionally We imparted the water of knowledge through the glance of Our eye and brow.

order.why: Attend to the suffering endured for education.
Read the series of purposes named for those ordeals.
Connect individual purity and the progress of the world.
shortened: The Prophets and Messengers of God have been sent down for the sole purpose of guiding mankind to the straight Path of Truth. The purpose underlying Their revelation hath been to educate all men, that they may, at the hour of death, ascend, in the utmost purity and sanctity and with absolute detachment, to the throne of the Most High. The light which these souls radiate is responsible for the progress of the world and the advancement of its peoples. They are like unto leaven which leaveneth the world of being, and constitute the animating force through which the arts and wonders of the world are made manifest.

order.why: Consider education as the shared purpose of the Messengers.
shortened: For what purpose did God send Moses? For what object did Christ appear? What was the mission of His Holiness Mohamad? Why did His Holiness the Bab step forth upon the arena of the world? For what cause did His Holiness Baha'u'llah manifest Himself? The answer is: The appearance of all these divine men is for no other reason save the education of the world of humanity.
Through this education the drop may become a sea, the atom find the importance of the sun, the extinguished lamp become the brilliant star and the wild tree a fruitful one.

order.why: Keep the comparison with philosophers in its reported setting.
shortened: Some philosophers, who were among the divine philosophers, were capable of causing fellowship to exist among a certain number of people, although the fellowship was outward and temporary; but they were unable to establish universal education, but the Holy Divine Manifestations of God accomplished universal education. They united the East and the West. They improved the morals of man. They changed the thoughts of man. They transformed the conduct of man.

order.why: Read the call to search for reality beyond superficial signs.
shortened: Where is the universal Reformer? For the dispelling of these darknesses there must needs be a Light. Now investigate day and night so that you may discover the source of this Light! It is well-known that the powers of philosophy and politics are unable to unite various nations and communities. Search then, for this source of illumination. Wherever you find there are the signs of Fire, turn your face toward it without hesitation. Be thou an admirer of reality and give no heed to superficialities. Love thou the Kernel and not the shell.

order.why: Consider the reported distinction between material and divine education.
shortened: The heart of man is a garden. The real garden is in order, well planted, watered and cultivated. This is not so with the jungle. The jungle gives no evidence of cultivation. Where there is no gardener disorder prevails. Wild growth produces nothing.
But the supreme education is Divine Teaching. Through it the most ignorant become wise and the lowest are elevated to the loftiest heights.
One day's education under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit is better than ten years material training in the universities of the world.
Baha'u'llah has said two steps are necessary for human development;--Material and Divine Education.

order.why: Hear the emphasis on the influence of training.
shortened: Training has a great effect, a profound influence.
All the Prophets were sent for the purpose of education. In brief, education is the cause of life, education is the cause of salvation, education is the cause of exalted stations.

order.why: Make room for moral learning by slow degrees.
shortened: If you want to educate a person you must strive for many years, exhorte him, advise him and train him with much difficulty. This is one kind of teaching the souls through the inculcation of moral lessons by slow degrees. The other way is through the guidance of God and the descent of the Holy Spirit. When a person is taught through the love of God there will come over him a radical change and his moral life will be transformed instantaneously and his conduct and manners will become spiritual.

order.why: Read affection as a lesson in the school of love.
shortened: Thou didst speak and thread pearls, and praise be to God, thou didst sweep the house of the heart clean of the straws and twigs of heedlessness and forgetfulness, and in the school of love, from the Divine Teacher, thou didst learn the lesson of affection.

order.why: Let acquired knowledge become a means of consolation.
shortened: Therefore you must not rest or be still day or night, engage in acquiring divine knowledge, and in the school of truth learn lessons from the teacher of love so that you may become the cause of consolation to these yearning ones.

order.why: Hear the names Comforter, Consoler, and Educator together.
shortened: He, in truth, is the Comforter and the Consoler, the true Educator and spiritual Master.

order.why: Read refreshment, eloquence, peace, and freedom as educational fruits.
Consider the learner becoming a source of guidance to others.
shortened: God sent His Prophets into the world to teach and enlighten man, to explain to him the mystery of the Power of the Holy Spirit, to enable him to reflect the light, and so in his turn, to be the source of guidance to others.

order.why: Connect teaching children with following the Prophets’ example.
Read the nurturing of children as more than physical parenthood.
shortened: Since you were an integral part of him, God willing, through divine assistance and grace, you will nurse his offspring at the breast of the love of God, give them to drink from the fountainhead of the knowledge of God, and nurture them in the cradle of care, so that these two branches may manifest the perfections of their root, and may truly be the progeny of his heart and soul rather than mere children of water and clay.

order.why: Consider a particular school’s moral and spiritual purpose.
shortened: I beseech God that in this school on Sundays you may acquire heavenly knowledge and receive divine moral education. Day by day may you progress until each one becomes a peerless sapling in the divine garden, full of leaves and blossoms and fruits.

order.why: Enter the image of the school of the spirit.
Read the Kingdom as a divine school.
shortened: O ye friends of 'Abdu'l-Baha! The reality of the Kingdom, which hath become manifest in this holy age at the center of all possibilities, is in truth a divine school, and the Educator of this heavenly school is the Blessed Beauty - may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones.

order.why: Hear the prayer for training and assistance.
Keep the personal encouragement to become worthy.
End the linked sequence with a prayer for guidance, unity, and felicity.
Retain the supplied summary of the prophetic mission.
Consider differences in capacity alongside the influence of education.
Keep the historical discussion of human origins in its stated theological setting.
shortened: We don't believe man has always had the form of man, but rather that from the outset he was going to evolve into the human form and species and not be a haphazard branch of the ape family. You see our whole approach to each matter is based on the belief that God sends us divinely inspired Educators. What they tell us is fundamentally true; what science tells us today is true, tomorrow may be entirely changed to better explain a new set of facts.

order.why: End with the challenge of language, audience, and expanded understanding.
shortened: The Manifestation of God (and, to a lesser degree, 'Abdu'l-Baha and Shoghi Effendi,) has to convey tremendous concepts covering the whole field of human life and activity to people whose present knowledge and degree of understanding are far below His. He must use the limited medium of human language against the limited and often erroneous background of His audience's traditional knowledge and current understanding to raise them to a wholly new level of awareness and behaviour. It is a human tendency, against which the Manifestation warns us, to measure His statements against the inaccurate standard of the acquired knowledge of mankind. We tend to take them and place them within one or other of the existing categories of human philosophy or science while, in reality, they transcend these and will, if properly understood, open new and vast horizons to our understanding.

questions: What changes when education is understood as bringing latent capacities into expression?
How do material livelihood, intellectual discovery, moral character, and spiritual life relate in these readings?
What signs in conduct would show that the education described here is taking effect?
How does Matthew 11:28–30 join learning with meekness and care for the burdened?
How can readers examine the historical examples carefully while engaging the larger argument about human development?
What might it mean to become a source of guidance or consolation after receiving education oneself?

references.label: 1 · Matthew 11:28–30 · Learning from meekness
references.note: In the King James Version, Jesus invites those who labor under burdens to come, learn from Him, and find rest. His description of meekness and lowliness gives the teacher’s character a central place. Compare this with the compilation’s images of nurture, consolation, and moral transformation, while attending to the different scope and setting of each account of education.

subjects.displayTitle: Spiritual springtime: renewal and the work of responding
subjects.introduction: Last year’s spring is now only a story; the freshness itself is gone. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá uses that plain fact to pose the harder question of whether we recognise a season while it is still here. When a Manifestation of God appears, He teaches, the rain, sun and breeze of a divine springtime pass over the world, and what returns to life is not a new set of doctrines but the old human virtues, purity, humility, patience and constancy, which had survived only as outward forms. Some trees blossom in that season and some, being dry, do not; growth is gradual; and the Nightingale will one day fly from its earthly nest, so the time to listen is now. Qur’án 57:17 links God’s reviving of the earth after its death with the making clear of His signs so that people may understand [1], and the Writings make the visible world a mirror of the spiritual. From here the journey continues into the cycles of the physical and spiritual worlds, the renewal of religion through progressive revelation, and the sense in which each age receives teachings that are its own spirit.
