subjects.arc: Begin with the difference between remembering and receiving spring, explore recurring revelation, and return to attention, growth, and the fruits of renewal.

order.why: Read recurring spring through continuity and increasing capacity.
Open with the difference between a remembered season and a present opportunity.
shortened: Consider that the last year's springtime is past and all that thou mayest say or hear (about it) is but a story (or narrative); but appreciate thou this New Year's Spring--which is this present time-hath pitched its tent with the utmost magnificence in the field and plain and hath made the mountain and desert verdant and fresh, hath made the trees to appear pure and fresh, blooming with flowers and blossoms through the vernal bounty and caused them to bring forth pure fruits.

order.why: Identify human virtues as the substance renewed.
shortened: It is purity, detachment, humility, forbearance, patience, and constancy. These are divine qualities. These commandments will never be abrogated, but will remain in force and effect for all eternity. These human virtues are renewed in every Dispensation; for at the close of each Dispensation the spiritual law of God, which consists in the human virtues, vanishes in substance and persists only in form.

order.why: Allow the new cycle’s capacities to unfold gradually.
shortened: Now in this world of being, the Hand of Divine Power hath firmly laid the foundations of this all-highest Bounty and this wondrous Gift. Gradually whatsoever is latent in the innermost of this Holy Cycle shall appear and be made manifest, for now is but the beginning of its growth and the dayspring of the revelation of its Signs.

order.why: Ask what fruits the renewed season calls forth.
Distinguish receiving gifts from becoming conscious of them.
Consider differing responses within the same season.
Introduce the appearance of Manifestations as spiritual springtime.
Read the extended analogy between material and spiritual cycles.
shortened: The vernal season has rain-laden clouds and musk-scented breezes, life-giving zephyrs and perfectly mild weather.  The rain falls, the sun shines, the reviving winds blow, the world is renewed, and the breath of life reveals itself in plant, animal and man alike.

The spiritual cycles associated with the Prophets of God proceed in like manner. That is, the day of the advent of the Holy Manifestations is the spiritual springtime. It is divine splendour and heavenly grace; it is the wafting of the breeze of life and the dawning of the Sun of Truth.
The spiritual cycles of the Sun of Truth, like the cycles of the physical sun, are in a state of perpetual motion and renewal.

order.why: Consider the Holy Spirit as mediator of renewed life.
shortened: The fifth degree of spirit is the Holy Spirit, which is the mediator between God and His creation.

Whensoever it appears the world is revived, a new cycle is ushered in, and the body of humanity is clothed in a fresh attire. It is like the spring: when it arrives it transports the world from one condition to another.

order.why: Read recreation through the Manifestations and divine mercy.
shortened: In every age and cycle He hath, through the splendorous light shed by the Manifestations of His wondrous Essence, recreated all things, so that whatsoever reflecteth in the heavens and on the earth the signs of His glory may not be deprived of the outpourings of His mercy, nor despair of the showers of His favors.

order.why: Place renewal within the source’s account of enduring creation.
Keep the account of ancient cycles and lost records in its theological setting.
shortened: Each of the Manifestations of God has likewise a cycle wherein His religion and His law are in full force and effect. When His cycle is ended through the advent of a new Manifestation, a new cycle begins. Thus, cycles are inaugurated, concluded, and renewed, until a universal cycle is completed in the world of existence and momentous events transpire which efface every record and trace of the past; then a new universal cycle begins in the world, for the realm of existence has no beginning.

order.why: Read the repeated fruit of the tree of life.
Distinguish lasting divine purpose from transient achievements.
shortened: In this mortal world every important matter hath an end; and every remarkable achievement a termination; none having permanent existence. For instance, consider how the important achievements of the ancient world have been totally exterminated and not a trace remaineth therefrom save the great Cause of the Kingdom of God, which hath no beginning and will have no end. At most, it is only renewed.

order.why: Consider the successive periods of a spiritual cycle.
Hear spring and autumn within a recurring sequence.
Read the related account of religion’s seasons.
Follow the movement from dormancy toward a renewed world.
shortened: When the divine spring is over and the heavenly bounty ceases, the trees of being lie dormant. Lifelessness and stillness prevail over the world of man. People become spiritless and withered. Autumn and winter set in. There exists no flower or greenery, no cheerfulness or mirth, no happiness or joy.

Then the spiritual spring spreads its tent once more. The gardens of the hearts regain their freshness, charm and verdure. The buds of knowledge open and the anemones of reality appear. The world of man becomes another world,

order.why: Ask whether one past spring could suffice for all time.
Keep the statement that a springtime does not remain unchanged forever.
Read the wedding feast and the seasons to come.
Attend to the source’s account of the interval between spiritual springs.
shortened: The outward spring -- unto which, by the command of the Creator of Names, the training of the outward forms of things is committed and entrusted -- appeareth but once in the year. Even so the spiritual spring, which nurtures souls and illumined hearts, and bestoweth the everlasting, enduring life, revealeth itself but once in a thousand years, or more; and upon all things, in the realms of the seen and the unseen, it conferreth the robe of existence and the splendor of lordship.

order.why: Hold continuing bounty beside the portion given to a particular time.
shortened: Listen with heart and soul to the songs of the spirit, and treasure them as thine own eyes; for heavenly wisdoms, even as vernal showers, will not rain forever upon the earth of men's hearts, and though the grace of the All-Bounteous One is never ceasing and never stilled, yet to every time and era a portion is allotted and a bounty assigned, which is vouchsafed in a given measure.

order.why: Read the urgency of hearing the Nightingale while its song is present.
shortened: The day will surely come when the Nightingale of Paradise will have winged its flight away from its earthly abode unto its heavenly nest. Then will its melody be heard no more, and the beauty of the rose cease to shine. Seize the time, therefore, ere the glory of the divine springtime hath spent itself, and the Bird of Eternity ceased to warble its melody, that thy inner hearing may not be deprived of hearkening unto its call.

order.why: Hear the related invitation to value days of meeting.
shortened: Know the value of these days, for union is not always possible. The nightingale singeth only in spring and crieth not until it seeth the rose. The time cometh when the divine nightingale ceaseth from mentioning meanings and taketh flight to the spiritual branch and settleth in the divine invisible rose gardens.

order.why: Consider the invitation to gather the fruits with one’s own hands.
Make room for the regret of an opportunity missed.
Enter the joyful imagery of creation awakened.
shortened: Then the bright dawn rose, and there came tidings of great joy. The divine springtime was here, pitching its tents in this contingent world, so that all creation leapt and danced. The withered earth brought forth immortal blooms, the dead dust woke to everlasting life. Then came forth flowers of mystic learning, and, bespeaking the knowledge of God, fresh greenery from the ground. The contingent world displayed God's bounteous gifts, the visible world reflecting the glories of realms that were hidden from sight.

order.why: Hear the songs and fragrances of inner meanings.
shortened: In flower-spangled meadows hath the divine springtime pitched its tents, and the spiritual are inhaling sweet scents from the Sheba of the spirit, carried their way by the east wind. Now doth the mystic nightingale carol its odes, and buds of inner meaning are bursting into blossoms delicate and fair.

order.why: Read the prayer’s rich sequence of restored life.
shortened: Through the life of mercy hast Thou revived these regions and domains. Thus have the meadows been adorned, the fountains made to flow, and the groves embellished through a ceaseless downpour from the clouds of grace and bounty. From the wafting breeze of Thy loving-kindness hath come a gentle wind, vivifying to souls and hearts. The lands have turned green, the trees have brought forth leaves, flowers have been made to bloom, fruits have ripened, the anemones of inner reality have opened wide, birds have broken into song, and eyes have been gladdened by beholding these signs.

order.why: Consider light, breeze, and rain working together.
Hear the proclamation of a changed world through spring imagery.
shortened: Soon the whole world, as in springtime, will change its garb. The turning and falling of the autumn leaves is past; the bleakness of the wintertime is over. The new year hath appeared and the spiritual springtime is at hand. The black earth is becoming a verdant garden; the deserts and mountains are teeming with red flowers; from the borders of the wilderness the tall grasses are standing like advance guards before the cypress and jessamine trees; while the birds are singing among the rose branches like the angels in the highest heavens, announcing the glad-tidings of the approach of that spiritual spring, and the sweet music of their voices is causing the real essence of all things to move and quiver.

order.why: Read renewal as the beginning of a new creation.
shortened: After the coming of the spiritual springtime, the falling of the vernal showers, the shining of the Sun of Reality, the blowing of the breezes of perfection, all phenomena become imbued with the life of a new creation and are reformed in the process of a new genesis.
When the holy, divine Manifestations or Prophets appear in the world, a cycle of radiance, an age of mercy dawns. Everything is renewed.

order.why: Bring the image into the gardens of human hearts.
Consider new life and divine qualities within the soul.
Hear hope rising with the stirring of the earth of souls.
Read the brief declaration that winter has passed.
shortened: Praise be to God! The dark and gloomy winter hath passed and the springtide of divine mercy hath adorned the world in a new raiment.

order.why: Consider joy through the manifestation of light.
Connect the new age with friendship and awakened consciences.
shortened: In this radiant century and merciful age the ears are open, hearts awakened, eyes seeing, consciences stirred. The age of estrangement has passed. The century of friendship has arrived. The dark hours have disappeared and the Orb of Unity has dawned.

order.why: Read the Cause’s youth through the conduct asked of its followers.
shortened: O loved ones of God! The religion of the All-Merciful is in the days of its youth, and this wondrous Cause is in the season of its springtime.

Open, then, the ear of understanding to the counsels and admonitions of God, and with sincerity of purpose, purity of nature, goodness of disposition, and loyal devotion to the state, manifest a shining hand, that it may be firmly established and clearly demonstrated in the assemblage of the world and the concourse of nations that ye are the radiant candle of the world of humanity and the rose of the garden of the divine world.

order.why: Keep the reference to the first century in its historical occasion.
shortened: O divine friends! His honor Nazim had written a letter mentioning the divine friends, and therefore the heart of Abdul-Baha was moved and stirred, and remembering those loving friends, engaged in this remembrance and utterance: O divine friends! This is the spiritual springtime and the divine spring season. This is the first century of the Ancient Beauty and the great cycle of the Greatest Name.

order.why: Consider a new year as an image of a new cycle.
Read Naw-Ruz through life-giving light.
Describes Revelation as a new springtime that renews the world.
Keep the seasonal description within its symbolic and geographical setting.
Read the equinox as the source’s symbol of the Messenger.
Consider the reported distinction between two equinoxes.
Hear the renewed life of meadows and orchards.
Read the energy of the vernal season as an analogy for human renewal.
shortened: This time of the world may be likened to the equinoctial in the annual cycle. For, verily, this is the spring season of God.

At the time of the vernal equinox in the material world a wonderful vibrant energy and new life-quickening is observed everywhere in the vegetable kingdom; the animal and human kingdoms are resuscitated and move forward with a new impulse. The whole world is born anew, resurrected.
Likewise, the spiritual bounty and springtime of God quicken the world of humanity with a new animus and vivification.

order.why: Consider consummation followed by a new condition.
shortened: According to an intrinsic law all phenomena of being attain to a summit and degree of consummation, after which a new order and condition is established.

order.why: Let the cold months and clouds lead toward growth and repose.
Hear the direct address announcing spring.
Read the showers of mercy and new bounty.
Consider the lower world as a mirror of virtues.
Retain the concise declaration of a new outpouring.
shortened: This is the outpouring of the wonderful and new springtime and the falling of the showers of the Bounty of the Most Great Lord!"

order.why: Hear the invitation to enter the garden.
Read sacrifice and gladness within the season’s imagery.
Consider the saplings’ leaves and fruits.
Attend to the particular beauty and consolation of varied plants.
shortened: O ye tender seedlings in the garden of the love of God!
O ye fresh saplings in the meadows of the knowledge of God!

The sight of the flowering plants in a springtime garden is delightful. The new-grown herbs shed abroad their pungent fragrances, each blossom charms the eye with its particular beauty, while the leaves and fruit are speedily burgeoning. And when people find their way into the garden and gaze on the beauty of the flowers, they inhale the perfume, their souls are exhilarated and their hearts are solaced.

order.why: Read the distinct image of the springtime of youth.
shortened: In the springtime of youth and the prime of life, whosoever attaineth unto the love of God is accounted among the denizens of the most exalted Paradise.

order.why: Consider the new garments of trees and gardens.
Hear the all-encompassing bounty described through flourishing fields.
Read the transformation of earth through rain.
Consider the rain falling upon noble and lowly alike.
shortened: O rose adorned and blossoming in the gardens of the love of God! The springtime has come, and the lofty clouds have poured down their copious rain upon both noble and lowly alike. The breezes of God have wafted over the gardens of earth and heaven with a new spirit, and the heat of the Sun of Truth has intensified upon every goodly plant and graceful tree growing in blessed soil from every clime.

order.why: Hear the concise gathering of cloud, sun, and breeze.
Keep the future hope of spring beside declarations of its arrival.
Read waiting through winter in the reported counsel.
Consider the expectation of signs of renewed life.
End the linked sequence with early, particular signs of growth.
shortened: The progress of the Cause is like unto the coming of the spring and its early signs. Suddenly one sees here a tree is putting forth leaves, another bush is being adorned with roses, the nightingales are singing and the meadows are green.

order.why: Retain the supplied image of progress through rhythmic trials and divine power.

questions: How does the difference between remembering a past spring and receiving a present one illuminate religious renewal?
What is renewed when enduring human virtues have survived mainly as outward forms?
How can divine bounty be continuing while a particular opportunity still asks for timely response?
What does the image of gradual growth suggest about expectations for personal and social transformation?
How does Qur’an 57:17 connect renewed life with understanding, and how is that connection developed here?
What fruits in thought, relationships, or service might indicate that a season of renewal is being received?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 57:17 · Reviving the earth and awakening understanding
references.note: Pickthall’s translation joins God’s reviving of the earth after its death with the making clear of revelation so that people may understand. Compare this brief connection with the compilation’s extended springtime imagery. Consider how the visible world can become an invitation to reflection, and how the Baha’i passages apply the image to the renewal brought by the Manifestations.

subjects.displayTitle: Kingship: justice, shared responsibility, and lasting sovereignty
subjects.introduction: Your people are your treasures, Bahá’u’lláh tells the kings of the earth, rebuking them for laying ever heavier burdens on their subjects to rear palaces for themselves. Kingship so understood is a trust, and justice, the most excellent garment for the temple of sovereignty, is the only thing that makes a king a sign of divine power. The same voice that calls a just king the lamp of the world also welcomes the republican form and foresees a day when no one will consent to bear alone the weight of kingship; ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, in turn, hopes that government and people may blend like milk and honey. Deuteronomy sets Israel’s king under a law that forbids him horses, wives and hoarded wealth and requires him to read that law daily so that his heart is not lifted above his brothers [1]. Beneath the thrones runs another sovereignty altogether, the kingdom of hearts won by service. From here the inquiry leads into the relationship between government and people, obedience to authority, and the proclamation addressed to kings.
subjects.arc: Begin with the welfare of the people, examine justice and shared government, and place temporal power beside the sovereignty of service.

order.why: Read government as a trust to protect the downtrodden.
shortened: God hath committed into your hands the reins of the government of the people, that ye may rule with justice over them, safeguard the rights of the downtrodden, and punish the wrongdoers.
Thou art God's shadow on earth. Strive, therefore, to act in such a manner as befitteth so eminent, so august a station.

order.why: Open with the people as the ruler’s treasures.
shortened: Fear the sighs and tears of this Wronged One, and lay not excessive burdens on your peoples.  Do not rob them to rear palaces for yourselves; nay rather choose for them that which ye choose for yourselves.

Your people are your treasures.  Beware lest your rule violate the commandments of God, and ye deliver your wards to the hands of the robber.  By them ye rule, by their means ye subsist, by their aid ye conquer.

order.why: Make justice the stated meaning of a king’s relation to divine power.
shortened: Kings are the manifestations of divine power, and what is intended is their justice - if they observe this, they are related to the Truth.

order.why: Identifies justice and wisdom as the strongest supports of a ruler.
Consider justice as the most excellent garment of sovereignty.
Read the just ruler through the image of a lamp.
Consider the head and body as an image of responsibility.
Examine the proposed combination of republican benefit and kingship.
Keep the related quotation within its reported conversation.
Consider maturity through unwillingness to bear kingship’s burden alone.
shortened: In one of the Tablets it was revealed that among the signs of the world's maturity is that no one will accept to bear alone the weight of kingship. Sovereignty will remain, but none will be willing to bear alone its burden. Those will be the days when wisdom will be manifest among mankind, save for him who may take on this mighty weight for the sake of propagating God's Cause and spreading His Faith.

order.why: Read the limits of governing vast territories from one center.
shortened: In reality it is not just that vast countries should be governed from a single center, for no matter how great the ability and wisdom of the statesmen of that center, or how developed their sense of justice, they will still not be fully informed of the needs of every town and village and cannot exert themselves justly for the betterment of their surrounding dependencies.

order.why: Join the welfare of government and nation.
Keep the reported sharing of administration within its historical occasion.
Read the description of constitutional England as a historical appraisal.
Consider the account of royal dignity with distributed burdens.
Attend to the specific circumstances of constitutional adjustment.
Read the need for capacity and responsibility in constitutional government.
shortened: The inhabitants of a nation must intelligently fulfill the requirements of the constitutional government and abide by all its conditions, otherwise it will bring upon them greater lawlessness and disintegration; for the reins will be taken out of the hands of an able, absolute Monarch and placed into the hands of a number of self-interested, useless parasites.

order.why: Keep the reported remarks on constitutions and punishment within their governmental setting.
shortened: It is impossible that a despotic government could make any progress in these days. All the kings of the world were at first despotic, but later they have become either constitutional or republican. Even some of the kings, by their own will, granted a constitution; such as the Mikado of Japan, who willingly granted one, and two years ago the Ameen of Montenegro, in Turkish Europe, also granted one. Why? Because today a despotic government cannot be held any more, and until the Royalist and Nationalist can become blended as milk and sugar, tranquility and prosperity cannot be obtained, and further, you must proceed to punish those who martyred one of the Bahais, Seyid Yah Yah, in the city of Sirjan.

order.why: Consider the reported appeal for equal rights and a constitution.
Read the reported vision of future constitutional monarchy without elevating its authority.
Distinguish rulership of the earth from the domain of hearts.
Hear the refusal to claim a share of worldly dominion.
shortened: Say: O people! Sow not the seeds of discord among men, and refrain from contending with your neighbor, for your Lord hath committed the world and the cities thereof to the care of the kings of the earth, and made them the emblems of His own power, by virtue of the sovereignty He hath chosen to bestow upon them. He hath refused to reserve for Himself any share whatever of this world's dominion.

order.why: Consider the conditional language of divine power and recognition.
Read a sovereign turning toward a higher Sovereign.
shortened: Blessed be the king whose sovereignty hath withheld him not from his Sovereign, and who hath turned unto God with his heart.  He, verily, is accounted of those that have attained unto that which God, the Mighty, the All-Wise, hath willed.  Erelong will such a one find himself numbered with the monarchs of the realms of the Kingdom.

order.why: Attend to the written counsel concerning loyalty to just monarchs.
Keep the separate reported answer about tyranny distinct in status and context.
Read governmental authority in relation to preservation and tranquility.
shortened: That which is necessary today is obedience to government and adherence to wisdom. In truth, the reins of preservation, tranquility and assurance outwardly lie within the grasp of governmental authority. Thus hath God willed it and thus hath He ordained it.

order.why: Hear the specific counsel concerning the rulers of the realm.
Consider the account of order and the risks of its weakening.
shortened: The Lord of all worlds hath entrusted the order of countries and the security of paths to the effort of government and the power of sovereignty, and hath made the comfort of the subjects and the prosperity of the people dependent upon the influence and might of the kings of the world. Should there occur any weakening in this mighty force which preserves the life, happiness, comfort and peace of creation, the felicity of human life would be disturbed, and the base, vile, rejected and riffraff would become dominant and prevailing.

order.why: Read the particular appeal for protection amid political unrest.
shortened: All these matters arise from the weakness of the government. Therefore, we pray that God may grant strength and victory to the government. Soon you will observe that the government will gain strength, and when it acquires power to maintain order, these problems will be solved.

order.why: Read the instruction to speak of peace with restraint.
Join national strength with the condition of justice.
Keep the praise of reform in Iran within its historical address.
shortened: Today by the grace of God and the spiritual influence of His universal Manifestation, the fair-minded ruler of Iran has gathered his people into the shelter of justice, and the sincerity of the imperial purpose has shown itself in kingly acts. Hoping that his reign will rival the glorious past, he has sought to establish equity and righteousness and to foster education and the processes of civilization throughout this noble land, and to translate from potentiality into actuality whatever will insure its progress.

order.why: Read gratitude for protection of the oppressed.
Hear the particular prayer for a monarch’s success.
shortened: In any case, praise be to God, His Imperial Majesty shows utmost patience and resists oppression and tyranny with justice and fairness.
Pray that His Imperial Majesty may be victorious and triumphant and his enemies defeated and subdued, for truly he is a kind king and a benevolent monarch full of favors.

order.why: Keep the prayer for protection and established government in its setting.
Read the hope for the subjects’ comfort and prosperity.
Consider the reported royal journey and the response it prompted.
Hear the hope for the future of Iran’s rulers.
shortened: Although praise be to God, even now His Imperial Majesty is like a radiant moon in the eastern horizon - nay rather, a brilliant sun - yet it is hoped that in this cycle of the All-Merciful and divine age, the Lord of the worlds will place such a crown of bounty upon the heads of Iran's monarchs that its brilliant jewel will shine and radiate forever in the east of prosperity and the zenith of eternal heaven.

order.why: Connect the ruler’s understanding with reform of the realm.
Read the particular assessment of the Sultan’s conduct.
Keep the account of two responses to the Iranian claimant distinct.
Hear the prayer for protection amid a dispute with divines.
Read the historical praise of British statesmanship in its occasion.
Retain the separate critique of recognition in its own voice.
shortened: The Queen of London goes daily to church in the name of God and, in her own imagination, is occupied with the remembrance of God, yet God hath testified and doth testify to her heedlessness, for she is deprived of His recognition and is clinging merely to His name. And likewise are the other empresses of the world.

order.why: Distinguish the reported royal letter concerning the Bab from the narrator’s own counsel.
Consider the declaration concerning glory taken from kings and divines.
Keep the recollected prediction concerning the Qajar dynasty attributed.
Read the upheaval of wartime fortunes.
Consider the scope of power formerly held by rulers.
shortened: In former centuries kings and rulers have absolutely dominated millions of men and have been thereby enabled to carry out whatsoever they desire. If they willed to bestow happiness and peace, they could do so; and if they determined to inflict suffering and discomfort, they were equally capable.

order.why: Hear the reported protest against rulers’ comforts amid the people’s suffering.
Examine the reported pressures sustaining the competition in armaments.
shortened: The Emperors and Kings of Europe are so situated today that either by inclination or rivalry; political considerations or patriotic motives, geographical locations or fear of foreign invasion - cannot take an initiative in the Cause of Universal Peace and the reduction of armaments. So long as this mad competition exists amongst them they think they must go on increasing their Military and Naval budgets and pile destructive armaments upon armaments unt[il] millions of souls are crushed under its sheer weight.

order.why: Consider the stated unreadiness to acknowledge universal peace.
Read the establishment of peace as a ruler’s true duty.
Consider rulers’ participation in a wider deliberative assembly.
shortened: It is incumbent upon the kings and the spiritual  leaders of the world to lay fast hold on religion, inasmuch as through it the fear of God is instilled in all else but Him."

It would be preferable and more fitting that the highly honored kings themselves should attend such an assembly, and proclaim their edicts. Any king who will arise and carry out this task, he verily will, in the sight of God, become the cynosure of all kings. Happy is he, and great is his blessedness!

order.why: Hear the hope that authority will enable freedom and useful work.
Connect national progress with learning and practical service.
Acknowledge the burdens and anxieties surrounding kingship.
Distinguish temporary sovereignty from enduring spiritual life.
Read vanished crowns beside the possibility of lasting glory.
shortened: O two remnants of the ancients! The Kayanian kings possessed crowns and diadems and raised golden parasols, but what benefit was it? It did not endure. Some among them in the other world also raised the banner of eternal glory and became noble.

order.why: Consider the contrast between monarchs and an enduring luminous influence.
Read the reported contrast of Napoleon’s power and Christ’s kingdom.
shortened: The sovereignty of Napoleon ceased as soon as he died but the Kingdom of Christ is eternal. The former established his mortal kingdom with bloodshed and the sword while Christ established the Kingdom of God with the life-giving breaths of the Holy Spirit. Napoleon established his kingdom through the power of oppression while Christ established His through the power of the love of God. A hundred thousand Napoleons may be effaced but the Kingdom of Christ will remain forever.

order.why: Keep the reported meaning of spiritual kings and queens distinct.
shortened: In speaking of the kings and queens of earth, Abdul-Baha said: "Their glory is but temporal and mortal, for they are but rules of this ephemeral sphere, where all things change from day to day and finally pass away entirely: But the women and men who in the time of a divine Manifestation come forward to acknowledge and believe in Him become real kings and queens, whose reign, glory and dominion are immortal.

order.why: Hear the warning about the brief duration of possessions.
shortened: Say: O concourse of princes! Beware lest the veils of the world withhold you from the Lord of all men. That which ye possess shall perish in less than a moment and ye shall find yourselves in manifest loss.

order.why: Read service as the path to a different grandeur.
shortened: O King, if thou seekest royal grandeur and kingly glory, serve at the threshold of God and seek servitude at the Most Great Court. The glory of kings is like the abasement of subjects - but for a moment, and the surging ocean of their grandeur is merely a dewdrop. Their brilliant lamp is a dark and extinct morning, and their exalted star sets in the depths of a small grave.

order.why: Consider the reversal of sovereignty and servitude.
shortened: O servant of the friends of the Most Glorious Beauty, may my spirit be sacrificed for them! Kings are in truth enslaved servants, needy and destitute. The true sovereigns of the kingdom of real dominion are the servants of the loved ones of God and the bondsmen of the divine Threshold.

order.why: Read spiritual treasure beside outward wealth.
Hear the summons to become a guide within the realm of knowledge.
Compare official reception with lasting heartfelt friendship.
shortened: Consider what wonderful love is this that has been established between us through the Power of His Holiness Baha'u'llah! The Shah of Persia came twice to Stuttgart. Although he was a royal King he did not find one real heartfelt friend. The utmost was the government received him officially according to its long-established custom just as it would have received any other royal Personage. But [we] who were Prisoners for 40 yrs have come here and have found so many heartfelt, cordial friends whose love and affection are lasting and not temporary.

order.why: Retain the reported historical account of a king’s profession of faith.
shortened: On Sunday, wearing his crown and royal attire, he entered with all his ministers and representatives in their official dress. The king cast off his crown and prayed. Then he came out and announced that Christianity was universal. The monarchy continued in his family until Bonaparte's time when it became a republic.

order.why: Read the vision of monarchs approaching with flowers and humility.
shortened: I see the monarchs of earth, having removed their crowns, reverently, submissively and humbly, with tears flowing, carrying baskets of colorful flowers on their heads, approaching the Shrines of Baha’u’llah and the Bab. Much in the same way that Christ wore the crown of thorns on His head, the kings of earth will carry flowers to the Shrines.

order.why: Hear the related reported anticipation of pilgrimage.
shortened: In the future, on foot and holding bouquets of flowers above their heads and carrying wreaths, the monarchs of the earth will come on pilgrimage to the Sacred Shrines. "And will raise to the Supreme Concourse the voice of their fervent supplications and will lift to the Abha Kingdom the tone of their prayers that, 'They endured banishment, imprisonment and martyrdom for the comfort of the friends!

order.why: Consider crowns laid down at a sacred threshold.
shortened: The kings of earth, bareheaded, and the queens, will walk up the boulevard of the Shrine of the Bab carrying bouquets of flowers. They will prostrate themselves, kiss that Sacred Threshold and place their crowns on that ennobled earth.

order.why: Read the reported image of ships and visiting monarchs.
Hear the fuller account of pilgrimage and supplication.
shortened: Ships carrying the flag of "Ya Baha'u'l-Abha!" will anchor at the port [of Haifa] and kings will disembark. On foot and bareheaded, and with humility and modesty, and in a state of supplication and entreaty, chanting divine verses and prayers, they will attain to a visit of the Shrine of the Exalted One [the Bab].

order.why: End with the supplied prayer for the endurance of just sovereignty.

questions: What changes when a ruler’s people are understood as treasures and the protection of their rights becomes the measure of power?
How do the passages distinguish the dignity of kingship from oppression or extravagant expenditure?
What possibilities are opened by shared responsibility and the proposed combination of republican benefit with royal dignity?
How does Deuteronomy 17:14–20 connect royal power with limits, learning, and humility?
How can attention to occasion and source status help readers consider the varied statements on loyalty, tyranny, and future government?
What kind of sovereignty is attributed to service, and how might that challenge ordinary measures of political success?

references.label: 1 · Deuteronomy 17:14–20 · The king under a law
references.note: The King James Version places Israel’s king under restraints concerning horses, wives, and accumulated wealth, and requires continuing study and observance of the law so that he does not exalt himself above others. Read this beside the compilation’s concern for justice, public burdens, and humility. The passage belongs to its own covenantal setting; compare its account of responsibility without treating it as the same constitutional proposal.
